Subject: Post-call: region pinning / data residency follow-up

Hi John / Priya — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

Summary of ask:
- Primary requirement: ensure customer data for Acme Bank US-facing workflows remains in US regions (data residency / region pinning)
- Secondary: EU region support for EU customer subset, with cross-region failover only in explicit DR scenarios
- Requirements: limited PII retention (30/90 day policies to be defined), token-level logging for audit, and controls around backups

Action items we agreed:
1) I will share a short brief on how Redwood supports region pinning, cross-region failover behavior, and backup retention (attached).
2) Marissa will scope Dedicated vs Private options for your compliance team and provide estimated lead times and pricing bands.
3) Your security team to send the specific data residency questions (eg. encryption at rest keys, KMS residency, backup geo-constraints).

High-level answers to questions asked on the call:
- Region pinning: we can route requests to a pinned region (US or EU) at the tenant/route level; model artifacts can be replicated to target regions for failover with explicit replication policies.
- Cross-region failover: allowed but can be limited to DR mode only; configurable policy to prevent automatic failover except under manual/allowed conditions.
- Backups: persistent backups are encrypted and can be retained in-region; we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and can restrict backup geo-redundancy to single region on request.

Next steps: I attached a one-pager (region-pinning-brief.pdf) and our SOC 2 summary. Will follow up with a short technical note mapping your specific asks to config flags.

Thanks — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: region pinning / data residency follow-up

Thanks Rishi — helpful recap. A couple of clarifying questions from our side before we loop in InfoSec: 

1) For EU customer data: if we pin to EU, can we ensure model artifacts and cache are never replicated to US regions (even for warm standby)? We need a hard guarantee for certain regulated products.
2) Cross-region failover: you mentioned manual-only option. Is there an option for automated failover but only to a pre-authorized region (eg. EU->EU or US->US) and never across jurisdictions?
3) Backups: can we get a snapshot-level retention policy that enforces deletion after 90 days and destroys keys upon deletion? We want to avoid any residual copies in another region.

Also please confirm whether logs (audit/logging tokens) can be stored in a separate logging account with retention controls and whether Redwood supports pushing logs to our Splunk instance in the EU.

John
John Harris
Head of Cloud Platform, Acme Bank
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: John Harris <john.h@acmebank.com>, Priya Mehta <pmehta@acmebank.com>

Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: region pinning / data residency follow-up

John — great questions. Short answers below; attaching the brief + SOC2 summary with a few callouts. See attached: region-pinning-brief.pdf, redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

1) EU data hard guarantee: yes — for our Private and Dedicated offerings we can configure regional isolation so that model artifacts, KV caches, and persistent storage are confined to the selected region(s). For Hosted (shared tenancy) we offer strong region pinning but with limited replication for capacity; for regulated workloads we recommend Dedicated or Private.

2) Automated failover constraints: we support policy-driven failover. You can set: 
   - automatic failover within the same jurisdiction only (EU->EU, US->US)
   - manual-only cross-jurisdiction failover (requires an authorized action)
   - a hybrid where low-priority traffic is allowed to fail over automatically within jurisdiction while high-priority traffic requires manual approval.

3) Backups & key destruction: snapshots can be configured with in-region storage only. We support customer-managed KMS; when keys are rotated/deleted we can coordinate key destruction and attest to deletion. We will need to align on retention SLA (90 days) and on-provision a deletion workflow with evidence (audit logs).

4) Logging & audit export: yes — we can push audit logs to your Splunk or to an EU-hosted logging account via secure transfer. We also provide token-level logging controls and can redact PII at ingest with a configurable policy. For stronger controls we recommend Private deployment so logs never leave the customer-managed VPC.

Suggested next steps: 
- Marissa: prepare a short comparison (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) with compliance notes and rough pricing; include estimated lead times for Dedicated and Private.
- Rishi: schedule a technical call with your InfoSec (if OK, propose Tuesday 10am PT) to walk through KMS, backups, and logging export specifics.

Attaching region-pinning brief now.

— Rishi

John / Priya — looping to add timeline and next steps from the ops/solutions side.

Quick notes: 
- Hosted: fastest to go-live but for strict in-region non-replication guarantees we recommend Dedicated or Private.
- Dedicated: can be reserved capacity in US and EU; artifacts and backups can be restricted to region. Lead time: ~6-8 weeks to provision and validate (depending on capacity).
- Private: full control (on-prem or VPC) and best for stringent regulatory controls; lead time and cost higher (we can scope after a short readiness assessment).

I'll prepare the comparison doc and include a short checklist for InfoSec. Rishi — I can take the technical call Tuesday 10am PT and invite our Solutions Engineer (Vanessa) and Product Security (Aditya) to join. John / Priya — does that time work for you?
